C / PERSONAL PROJECTS

STOPLAB / When should learning stop?

Python / PyTorch / scikit-learn / Personal

Benchmarking the reliability of active-learning stopping rules under label noise and sampling bias

  • Reproduce prediction-stability stopping rules; evaluate sensitivity to label noise, class imbalance, and biased stop sets.
  • Measure premature stopping and excess labeling through repeated trials, ablations, and reproducible experiments.
Label budget / predictive performanceVisualization / demo to be added

STOPLAB is a planned benchmark for understanding when active-learning stopping rules fail. The project will compare prediction-stability criteria under label noise, class imbalance, and changes in stop-set composition. Repeated trials and controlled comparisons will separate premature stopping from unnecessary labeling. The interactive view will eventually expose those trade-offs directly.

SENSORLAB / Learning where to measure

Python / JAX / SciPy / Personal

Simulation-guided sensor placement for estimating thermal properties from sparse, noisy measurements

  • Develop a differentiable heat solver for material-parameter inference; verify gradients against finite differences.
  • Compare adaptive, uniform, and random sensor layouts using parameter error, uncertainty, and identifiability.
Thermal field / sensor placementVisualization / demo to be added

SENSORLAB is a planned study of how sensor placement affects the recovery of unknown thermal properties. A verified heat solver will generate controlled observations, allowing adaptive layouts to be compared with uniform and random placements under the same measurement budget. The emphasis is on parameter recovery, uncertainty, and the conditions under which the parameters can be identified.

LUMEN / CPU and GPU path tracer

C++ / CUDA / OpenGL / Planned

CPU/GPU path tracing for physically based lighting simulation

  • Implement BVH traversal and multiple importance sampling; extend a CPU reference tracer to a GPU wavefront pipeline.
  • Benchmark image error, throughput, and memory across scenes; verify convergence and CPU/GPU consistency.
Light transport / convergenceVisualization / demo to be added

LUMEN is a planned CPU/GPU path tracer for physically based lighting simulation. Development will begin with a CPU reference renderer, then explore a GPU wavefront pipeline. The eventual demo will connect sampling choices to visible image quality, while benchmarks compare convergence, throughput, and memory under matched conditions.
